controls.description: All manual journal entries above a defined threshold require approval by a person independent of the preparer before posting; approval is evidenced by signature or system workflow.
controls.evidence_of_operation: Journal approval log or workflow audit trail showing preparer, approver and timestamps.
controls.limitations: Does not prevent collusion between preparer and approver; management override can bypass it.
controls.objective: Prevent unauthorised or unsupported manual journals, the primary vehicle for management override.
controls.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

controls.description: A whistleblowing policy with a reporting channel independent of line management, communicated to all staff, with reports logged, investigated and reported to those charged with governance.
controls.evidence_of_operation: Policy document, communication records, log of reports received and investigation outcomes.
controls.limitations: Ineffective if staff do not trust the channel or fear retaliation; absence of reports does not prove absence of fraud.
controls.objective: Detect fraud and override by giving staff a safe route to report concerns.
controls.responsible_role: Those charged with governance / ethics officer
controls.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

controls.description: Staff in cash-handling, payment and recording roles are required to take periodic uninterrupted leave, with their duties performed by others during absence; key roles are rotated where feasible.
controls.evidence_of_operation: Leave records, handover notes, rotation schedule.
controls.limitations: Disruptive to operations; does not detect frauds that do not require the perpetrator's continuous presence.
controls.objective: Increase the chance that concealed misappropriation is exposed when someone else performs the role.
controls.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

controls.description: Significant accounting estimates are independently reviewed and challenged by someone without responsibility for preparing them, with the challenge documented, before the financial statements are finalised.
controls.evidence_of_operation: Review checklist or memo documenting assumptions challenged and conclusions reached.
controls.limitations: A reviewer who defers to management adds no assurance; challenge must be genuine and evidenced.
controls.objective: Detect and deter systematic management bias in estimates.
controls.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

controls.description: Revenue cut-off and recognition for material or unusual transactions are reviewed by a function independent of sales, with supporting dispatch and acceptance evidence inspected before revenue is recorded.
controls.evidence_of_operation: Cut-off checklist, review sign-off, matched dispatch/delivery evidence.
controls.limitations: Does not address fictitious sales supported by fabricated dispatch documents; depends on the reviewer's scepticism.
controls.objective: Prevent premature or fictitious revenue recognition driven by target pressure.
controls.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

evidence.contradictory_evidence: Journal population that does not reconcile to the general ledger movement in the period.
evidence.description: A complete extract of all manual journal entries for the period, obtained directly from the system, including preparer, approver, date, time, accounts and amounts.
evidence.expected_characteristics: Complete population (reconciled to GL movements), with system-generated timestamps and user IDs.
evidence.limitations: Only covers journals in the system; top-side or off-system adjustments are not captured.
evidence.name: Complete manual journal population extract
evidence.reliability_notes: High reliability for completeness when obtained directly by the auditor from the system and reconciled to the ledger; reliability falls if the auditor cannot verify the extract is complete.
evidence.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

evidence.contradictory_evidence: Journals posted without approval or with approval after the fact.
evidence.description: Approval records, supporting schedules and authorisation evidence for tested journal entries.
evidence.expected_characteristics: Approval by an independent person before posting, dated, with supporting documentation attached.
evidence.limitations: Approval may be perfunctory; the signature proves a control operated, not that it was effective.
evidence.name: Journal approval records and supporting documentation
evidence.reliability_notes: Internally generated; reliability depends on the approver's independence and competence. Approval after posting is a deficiency, not evidence of control operation.
evidence.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

evidence.contradictory_evidence: Actual outcomes consistently differing from estimates in the same direction.
evidence.description: Prior-period estimate working papers alongside the actual outcomes when they became known.
evidence.expected_characteristics: Dated working papers showing assumptions used; actual outcome data from reliable sources.
evidence.limitations: A single-period difference proves nothing; bias is assessed from a pattern, and hindsight must not be confused with bias at the time.
evidence.name: Prior-year estimate working papers and actual outcome data
evidence.reliability_notes: Working papers are internal and may reflect the bias under test; actual outcome data is more objective. The comparison itself is auditor-generated and therefore more reliable than either source alone.
evidence.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

evidence.contradictory_evidence: Transaction terms that make no commercial sense or counterparties that cannot be verified.
evidence.description: Contracts, correspondence, board approvals and commercial documentation supporting significant unusual transactions.
evidence.expected_characteristics: Executed agreements, evidence of negotiation, board or committee approval where required.
evidence.limitations: Documents can be fabricated to support a sham transaction; the auditor must remain sceptical of internally generated support.
evidence.name: Contracts and business correspondence for unusual transactions
evidence.reliability_notes: External contracts are more reliable than internal memos; reliability increases with corroboration from independent sources (e.g. counterparty confirmation).
evidence.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

evidence.contradictory_evidence: Count differences with no plausible explanation.
evidence.description: The auditor's independent record of cash counted and inventory test-counted without prior notice to the entity.
evidence.expected_characteristics: Recorded at the time, identifying denominations/items, locations, quantities and custodians.
evidence.limitations: A point-in-time procedure; does not address misappropriation that occurred and was concealed before the count date.
evidence.name: Surprise count records (cash and inventory)
evidence.reliability_notes: High reliability: obtained directly by the auditor through observation and inspection, and the surprise element reduces the opportunity for concealment.
evidence.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

evidence.contradictory_evidence: Transactions with parties later identified as related but undisclosed.
evidence.description: Shareholder registers, directorship records, board minutes and organisational charts used to identify related parties.
evidence.expected_characteristics: Current registers, signed minutes, complete organisational structure.
evidence.limitations: Deliberately concealed relationships may not appear in any of these sources.
evidence.name: Related-party registers and governance records
evidence.reliability_notes: Official registers are moderately reliable; board minutes are internal. Completeness of the related-party population is the key limitation - absence from these records does not prove a party is unrelated.
evidence.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

evidence.contradictory_evidence: Bank movements with no corresponding accounting entry.
evidence.description: Bank statements obtained directly from the bank and third-party confirmations of balances and arrangements.
evidence.expected_characteristics: Directly received from the bank, covering the full period, including confirmation of facilities and restrictions.
evidence.limitations: Confirms the bank's records, not the entity's completeness; collusion with bank staff is possible but rare.
evidence.name: Bank statements and confirmations obtained directly
evidence.reliability_notes: High reliability: external source, obtained directly by the auditor without passing through the entity.
evidence.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

evidence.contradictory_evidence: HR records showing the same person in incompatible roles with no compensating control.
evidence.description: HR records, role descriptions, leave records and organisation charts evidencing who performs incompatible functions.
evidence.expected_characteristics: Current job descriptions, leave taken records, documented compensating controls where segregation is absent.
evidence.limitations: Documents describe the intended design; actual practice may differ (enquiry and observation needed).
evidence.name: HR and role records evidencing segregation (or its absence)
evidence.reliability_notes: Internal records of moderate reliability; corroboration through observation of who actually performs the tasks increases reliability.
evidence.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

factor_risk.additional_info_needed: Whether any compensating controls exist (e.g. independent review of the person's work); the size of the entity and feasibility of segregation.
factor_risk.applicability: Applies where one person can initiate, record and conceal a transaction. Less applicable in very small entities where segregation is genuinely impracticable AND strong owner oversight with evidence exists.
factor_risk.confidence_basis: The fraud triangle: lack of segregation is the classic opportunity condition; combined with asset custody it enables both misappropriation and its concealment.
factor_risk.explanation: When the same person authorises transactions, records them and has custody of assets, no independent check stands between the act and its concealment. Errors and frauds alike can be hidden in the records the same person maintains.
factor_risk.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md
factor_risk.trigger_condition: One person performs incompatible functions (authorisation, recording, custody) without effective independent review.

factor_risk.additional_info_needed: How targets are set, whether they are realistically achievable, and the proportion of remuneration at risk.
factor_risk.applicability: Applies where targets are aggressive relative to the business outlook and rewards are material. Less applicable where targets are modest, independently set, and bonuses are a small part of remuneration.
factor_risk.confidence_basis: The fraud triangle: pressure to meet targets is the classic incentive condition for fraudulent financial reporting.
factor_risk.explanation: When management's rewards depend on hitting aggressive earnings targets, the incentive to report the desired outcome rather than the actual outcome increases. Revenue is the most common lever because it is visible and directly linked to targets.
factor_risk.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md
factor_risk.trigger_condition: Management remuneration is materially linked to aggressive, possibly unachievable earnings or revenue targets.

factor_risk.additional_info_needed: The business purpose of the structures, the identity of the counterparties, and whether transactions are on arm's-length terms.
factor_risk.applicability: Applies where structures or transactions lack a clear commercial rationale. Less applicable where related-party dealings are transparent, documented and independently approved.
factor_risk.confidence_basis: Opaque related-party structures are a recognised opportunity condition: they provide channels for off-book arrangements and round-tripping that are hard for the auditor to see.
factor_risk.explanation: Complex or opaque related-party structures give management a mechanism to move amounts in and out of the reported results - fictitious sales, concealed liabilities, or siphoned funds - while the accounting entries appear formally valid.
factor_risk.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md
factor_risk.trigger_condition: Related-party structures or transactions exist whose business purpose is unclear or undocumented.

factor_risk.additional_info_needed: Headroom under the covenants, the consequences of breach, and the timing of covenant tests relative to the reporting date.
factor_risk.applicability: Applies where covenants are tight or a breach would have severe consequences (acceleration, loss of funding). Less applicable where there is comfortable headroom and waivers are readily available.
factor_risk.confidence_basis: The fraud triangle: threatened loss of financing is a powerful pressure condition, and covenant tests create period-end incentives.
factor_risk.explanation: When breaching a covenant would trigger repayment demands or loss of facilities, management faces intense pressure to present compliant numbers at the test date. This pressure concentrates on period-end balances and the estimates that determine them.
factor_risk.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md
factor_risk.trigger_condition: Debt covenants or financing conditions are tight, with severe consequences for breach.

factor_risk.additional_info_needed: Reasons for departures, length of vacancies, and whether handovers were documented.
factor_risk.applicability: Applies where turnover affects financial reporting roles and knowledge is lost. Less applicable where departures are planned, handovers documented, and cover is competent.
factor_risk.confidence_basis: Instability in finance weakens the control environment and creates opportunity: new or temporary staff are less likely to challenge irregularities and more likely to process what they are given.
factor_risk.explanation: Frequent changes in finance personnel erode institutional knowledge, weaken review disciplines, and create gaps in which irregular entries or missing reconciliations go unchallenged. It can also signal an unhealthy environment that itself reflects pressure.
factor_risk.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md
factor_risk.trigger_condition: Unusually high turnover or prolonged vacancies in finance and key accounting roles.

factor_risk.additional_info_needed: Specific examples of the aggressive positions taken and how they compare with the applicable financial reporting framework.
factor_risk.applicability: Applies where management's justifications are vague appeals to practice rather than to the requirements of the framework. Less applicable where positions are well-reasoned and documented against the standards.
factor_risk.confidence_basis: The fraud triangle: rationalization is the internal justification that lets people commit fraud while preserving their self-image; a culture of normalising aggressive accounting is its observable form.
factor_risk.explanation: When management routinely defends aggressive accounting as 'what everyone does', it signals a culture in which the boundary between aggressive and improper has blurred. This attitude predicts both biased estimates and tolerance of override.
factor_risk.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md
factor_risk.trigger_condition: Management justifies aggressive accounting choices by appeal to industry practice rather than the reporting framework.

factor_risk.additional_info_needed: The business reasons for cash intensity, who handles cash, and what independent checks exist.
factor_risk.applicability: Applies where cash volumes are material and oversight is weak. Less applicable where cash is immaterial or subject to daily independent reconciliation and surprise counts.
factor_risk.confidence_basis: Cash is the most portable asset; weak oversight over large cash flows is a direct opportunity condition for misappropriation.
factor_risk.explanation: Large cash volumes that are not independently reconciled or verified create a direct opportunity to divert funds. Cash leaves little trail, so diversion can continue undetected and be concealed with falsified records.
factor_risk.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md
factor_risk.trigger_condition: Material cash transactions occur without independent reconciliation, review or verification.

factor_risk.additional_info_needed: Whether a channel exists on paper but is unused, and staff perceptions of retaliation risk.
factor_risk.applicability: Applies where no channel exists or where staff do not trust it. Less applicable where an independent, well-used channel with evidenced follow-up exists.
factor_risk.confidence_basis: A trusted reporting channel is a key detective control over fraud; its absence removes a deterrent and a detection route, increasing opportunity.
factor_risk.explanation: Fraud is most often detected through tips. Without a trusted channel, employees who observe wrongdoing have no safe route to report it, so frauds - particularly those involving management - can continue indefinitely.
factor_risk.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md
factor_risk.trigger_condition: No whistleblowing channel exists, or staff do not trust the channel that exists.

factors.conditions_relevant: Relevant in any entity where transaction volumes or staffing make segregation feasible. In very small entities, assess whether owner oversight genuinely compensates.
factors.description: The same individual can authorise transactions, record them in the books, and has physical or system custody of the related assets - with no independent review of their work.
factors.name: Lack of segregation of duties
factors.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md
factors.warning_signs: One person controls ordering, receiving and payment; journal preparer also approves journals; reconciliations prepared and reviewed by the same person; prolonged absence of leave taken by key staff.

factors.conditions_relevant: Relevant where targets materially affect remuneration or reputation and are set at levels that stretch plausibility given the business outlook.
factors.description: A dominant chief executive or small management group sets aggressive earnings or revenue targets, and a material part of their remuneration - or their standing with the board and market - depends on achieving them.
factors.name: Dominant management with aggressive earnings targets linked to bonuses
factors.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md
factors.warning_signs: Targets repeatedly set just above prior-year results; bonuses heavily weighted to a single metric; management dismisses missed forecasts as one-offs while celebrating narrow beats.

factors.conditions_relevant: Relevant where the group structure includes entities or transactions whose commercial purpose is not evident from the documentation.
factors.description: The entity uses complex, layered or opaque related-party structures, special-purpose vehicles, or circular transactions for which no clear business purpose is documented.
factors.name: Complex or opaque related-party structures with no clear business purpose
factors.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md
factors.warning_signs: Entities in low-transparency jurisdictions with no operational substance; transactions that net to little commercial effect; reluctance to explain structures; significant balances with undisclosed parties.

factors.conditions_relevant: Relevant where covenants are tested at or near the reporting date and headroom is thin.
factors.description: The entity faces significant pressure to satisfy debt covenants, maintain credit ratings, or meet conditions for continued financing, where failure would trigger repayment, higher costs or loss of facilities.
factors.name: Significant pressure to meet debt covenants or financing conditions
factors.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md
factors.warning_signs: Covenant headroom shrinking over successive periods; last-minute waivers or renegotiations; financing conditional on reported ratios; management focus on covenant calculations near period-end.

factors.conditions_relevant: Relevant where turnover affects financial reporting, internal audit or key control operators.
factors.description: There is unusually high turnover, prolonged vacancies, or heavy reliance on temporary staff in finance and key accounting roles.
factors.name: High turnover in finance and key accounting personnel
factors.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md
factors.warning_signs: Key roles vacant at period-end; reconciliations long outstanding; new staff unable to explain prior-period balances; exit interviews citing pressure or ethical concerns.

factors.conditions_relevant: Relevant where management's accounting choices sit at the aggressive end of acceptable practice.
factors.description: Management has a history of defending aggressive accounting positions by describing them as normal industry practice rather than by reference to the requirements of the financial reporting framework.
factors.name: Management history of justifying aggressive accounting as 'industry practice'
factors.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md
factors.warning_signs: Recurring disputes with auditors resolved in management's favour on thin reasoning; policies changed to the more aggressive permitted option; benchmarking against peers used to justify rather than to calibrate.

factors.conditions_relevant: Relevant where cash receipts or payments are material and the business model does not inherently require cash intensity.
factors.description: The entity handles large volumes of cash receipts or payments with weak oversight - cash not banked promptly, reconciliations not independent, and cash counts infrequent or predictable.
factors.name: Large volumes of cash transactions with weak oversight
factors.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md
factors.warning_signs: Cash banked late or in round sums; cash reconciliations prepared by the cashier; predictable count dates; lifestyle inconsistent with known income among cash handlers.

factors.conditions_relevant: Relevant in any entity; particularly important where management is dominant and other detective controls are weak.
factors.description: There is no whistleblowing or speak-up channel, or the channel that exists is not trusted by staff - for example reports go to the very managers whose conduct might be reported.
factors.name: Whistleblowing channel absent or not trusted
factors.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md
factors.warning_signs: No policy communicated to staff; channel administered by line management; no record of any report ever being made; staff survey or enquiry indicates fear of retaliation.

procedure_evidence.notes: Population extract is the starting point for stratification.
Approval records and support are inspected for the selected entries.
Surprise counts are one form of unpredictable procedure.
Direct bank confirmations at an unexpected date are another form.
Working papers and outcome data are the core evidence.
Contracts and correspondence are inspected for commercial substance.
Registers and minutes support the completeness search.
Count records are the primary output.
Direct bank evidence corroborates the cash position.
Registers, minutes and charts are searched for undisclosed parties.
Transaction documentation is scanned for related-party indicators.

procedures.exception_criteria: Material unsupported or unauthorised journals; journals that lack any business rationale; a pattern of period-end entries that consistently improve reported results.
procedures.expected_result: Tested journals are authorised, supported by valid business rationale, and correctly recorded; the stratification identifies no unexplained concentration of high-risk entries.
procedures.follow_up: Investigate each exception with management and corroborate explanations independently. If explanations are inadequate, extend testing to similar entries, quantify the potential misstatement, and reassess fraud risk - including whether those charged with governance need to be informed. Do NOT automatically conclude that fraud has occurred; consider escalation proportionate to the evidence.
procedures.objective: Detect manual journal entries used to manipulate reported results, including management override of controls.
procedures.population: All manual journal entries posted in the period (complete system extract, reconciled to the general ledger).
procedures.sampling_notes: Stratified selection, not random sampling: 100% of entries matching high-risk flags (period-end, outside hours, senior management, round amounts, seldom-used accounts, post-closing), plus a sample of the remainder.
procedures.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md
steps: Obtain a complete extract of manual journals directly from the system and reconcile the population to the general ledger movements.

Stratify the population using risk flags: entries posted at or after period-end, outside normal hours, by senior management, in round amounts, to seldom-used or sensitive accounts, and entries with blank or vague descriptions.
For selected entries, inspect supporting documentation, verify independent approval, and evaluate the business rationale.
Trace a sample of entries through to the financial statements to confirm correct recording.
procedures.title: Journal entry testing for management override

procedures.exception_criteria: Unpredictable procedures repeatedly uncover issues in areas previously tested clean, suggesting prior procedures were anticipated and circumvented.
procedures.expected_result: The varied procedures are performed as planned and their results are consistent with the rest of the audit evidence.
procedures.follow_up: Where unpredicted selections reveal issues, investigate fully and consider whether the pattern suggests deliberate concealment - reassess fraud risk and extend procedures accordingly, without presuming fraud.
procedures.objective: Reduce the risk that management anticipates audit procedures and conceals fraud in untested areas.
procedures.population: Varies by year: locations, balances, transaction streams and timing.
procedures.sampling_notes: Deliberately non-statistical: choose what was NOT covered last year and what management would least expect.
procedures.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md
steps: Vary the timing of procedures (e.g. interim vs year-end) compared with the prior year.
Select different locations, branches or business units from those covered previously.
Test account balances and transaction streams that were below the testing threshold last year.
Perform at least one procedure without forewarning the entity (e.g. a surprise count or an unannounced confirmation date).
procedures.title: Unpredictable audit procedures

procedures.exception_criteria: Estimates consistently resolved in the direction favourable to reported results, or assumptions repeatedly at the optimistic end of the range.
procedures.expected_result: Prior estimates proved reasonable in light of actual outcomes, with no systematic directional pattern.
procedures.follow_up: A pattern of optimistic outcomes is a bias indicator, not proof of fraud: discuss with management, challenge current-year assumptions with heightened scepticism, consider involving those charged with governance, and evaluate the aggregate effect on the financial statements.
procedures.objective: Identify indicators of systematic management bias in significant accounting estimates.
procedures.population: All significant accounting estimates from the prior period where outcomes are now known.
procedures.sampling_notes: Census of significant estimates; bias is assessed from the pattern across estimates, not from any single one.
procedures.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md
steps: List the significant estimates made in the prior period and the key assumptions behind each.
Compare each estimate with the actual outcome now known, quantifying the difference and its direction.
Assess whether differences cluster in the direction favourable to reported results.
Evaluate whether the pattern indicates bias affecting current-period estimates and challenge those assumptions accordingly.
procedures.title: Retrospective review of prior-year significant estimates

procedures.exception_criteria: Transactions with no discernible business purpose, circular cash flows, or counterparties that cannot be verified as independent.
procedures.expected_result: Each significant unusual transaction has a clear, documented business rationale consistent with the entity's strategy.
procedures.follow_up: Where rationale is absent or unconvincing, extend procedures: confirm terms with counterparties, inspect cash flows, and evaluate whether the transaction was designed to misstate the financial statements. Escalate to those charged with governance if management cannot explain the transaction. Do not presume fraud from an unusual transaction alone.
procedures.objective: Determine whether significant unusual transactions (especially with related parties) have genuine business substance or were structured to misstate the financial statements.
procedures.population: All transactions identified as significant and unusual (size, nature, timing, counterparty).
procedures.sampling_notes: Census of significant unusual transactions; professional judgment defines the threshold.
procedures.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md
steps: Identify significant transactions outside the normal course of business, near period-end, or with related parties.
Obtain and inspect the underlying contracts, approvals and correspondence.
Evaluate whether the terms, timing and economics make commercial sense.
Where applicable, confirm key terms directly with the counterparty and trace the cash flows.
procedures.title: Business-rationale testing of significant unusual transactions

procedures.exception_criteria: Unexplained shortages, cash or inventory that cannot be located, or records that do not match physical quantities.
procedures.expected_result: Physical quantities agree with records (subject to investigated differences); cash counted agrees with the book balance.
procedures.follow_up: Investigate all differences immediately while on site; if shortages are unexplained, extend counts, review access and custody records, and reassess fraud risk. Treat indicators as requiring investigation, not as conclusions.
procedures.objective: Obtain direct evidence of cash and inventory existence without giving the entity an opportunity to conceal shortages.
procedures.population: Cash on hand and physical inventory at selected locations.
procedures.sampling_notes: Unannounced timing; locations weighted toward weak oversight and high-value holdings.
procedures.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md
steps: Without prior notice, attend selected locations and take control of cash and inventory areas.
Count cash by denomination and test-count inventory in both directions, recording results independently.
Reconcile to the books on the spot and investigate differences immediately with custodians.
procedures.title: Surprise cash and inventory verification

procedures.exception_criteria: Undisclosed related parties identified; material transactions with parties whose relationship was concealed.
procedures.expected_result: The related-party population is complete; all identified relationships and material transactions are disclosed.
procedures.follow_up: For each newly identified party, identify all transactions and balances, evaluate disclosure, and consider why the party was undisclosed - concealment may indicate fraud risk elsewhere. Inform those charged with governance of the findings.
procedures.objective: Detect related-party relationships and transactions that management has not disclosed.
procedures.population: Shareholder and directorship registers, board minutes, organisational charts, and material transaction documentation.
procedures.sampling_notes: Targeted search, not sampling: follow names, addresses and shared officers across sources.
procedures.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md
steps: Inspect shareholder registers, directorship records and organisational charts for the full period.
Review board minutes for discussion of related parties and undisclosed arrangements.
Scan material contracts and transactions for related-party indicators (shared addresses, officers, non-arm's-length terms).
Cross-check findings against management's related-party listing and investigate omissions.
procedures.title: Related-party completeness search

risk_assertions.conditions: Relevant where journals record transactions or adjustments; fictitious entries overstate what occurred.
risk_assertions.why_relevant: Manipulative journals typically create or inflate recorded transactions that never occurred or did not occur as recorded.

risk_assertions.conditions: Relevant where journals reclassify amounts to conceal the true nature of transactions.
risk_assertions.why_relevant: Override often works through misclassification - moving amounts between accounts to hide losses, inflate revenue or bury expenses.

risk_assertions.conditions: Relevant where journals are posted at or after period-end to shift results between periods.
risk_assertions.why_relevant: Period-end journals are the classic mechanism for pulling results across the cut-off line.

risk_assertions.conditions: Relevant where assets are recorded at amounts that include diverted funds or fictitious balances.
risk_assertions.why_relevant: Misappropriated assets are gone but may still be carried in the books, or fictitious assets may be recorded to conceal the theft.

risk_assertions.conditions: Relevant where concealment involves omitting the loss or the liability it created.
risk_assertions.why_relevant: Falsified records conceal the diversion; the corresponding loss, or amounts owed, may never be recorded.

risk_assertions.conditions: Relevant where the carrying amount is not written down after the loss.
risk_assertions.why_relevant: Stolen or diverted assets held at full carrying amount overstate the balance sheet until written down.

risk_assertions.conditions: Relevant where sales are recorded without genuine underlying transactions.
risk_assertions.why_relevant: Fictitious revenue is, by definition, recorded transactions that did not occur.

risk_assertions.conditions: Relevant where genuine sales are pulled forward into the current period.
risk_assertions.why_relevant: Premature recognition records in this period transactions that belong in the next.

risk_assertions.conditions: Relevant where amounts are inflated through side agreements or channel stuffing.
risk_assertions.why_relevant: Inflated or grossed-up amounts overstate revenue even when some underlying transaction exists.

risk_assertions.conditions: Relevant wherever a significant estimate determines a carrying amount.
risk_assertions.why_relevant: Biased assumptions directly determine carrying amounts - provisions, impairments, fair values and revenue estimates.

risk_assertions.conditions: Relevant where the financial statements disclose the assumptions behind material estimates.
risk_assertions.why_relevant: Biased estimates are often accompanied by disclosures that present the assumptions as neutral; the disclosure itself may then be misleading.

risk_assertions.conditions: Relevant where biased estimates flow through profit or loss (e.g. provisions, depreciation).
risk_assertions.why_relevant: Systematic optimism in estimates misstates the amounts recognised in the period.

risk_controls.explanation: Independent journal approval is the primary preventive control over the manipulation mechanism.
A trusted reporting channel is often how override is first detected.
Tips are the most common detection route for asset misappropriation.
Rotation and mandatory leave expose concealed diversions that depend on the perpetrator's continuous presence.
Independent cut-off review directly addresses premature and fictitious revenue.
Staff may observe pressure to manipulate revenue before the auditor does.
Genuine independent challenge is the direct control over estimate bias.

risk_procedures.reason: Unpredictable procedures counter management's ability to anticipate revenue testing and hide fictitious sales in untested areas.
Biased estimates are often implemented through manual journals (e.g. provision top-ups); journal testing targets the mechanism.
Journals are the primary mechanism for both override and concealment of misappropriation.
Misappropriation is routinely concealed with falsified journals.
Fictitious and premature revenue is frequently created through period-end journals.
Unpredictability counters management's ability to anticipate and circumvent planned procedures.
Unannounced selections reduce the opportunity to conceal diverted assets.
A pattern of optimistic outcomes is the observable footprint of systematic bias.
Retrospective review can also reveal bias introduced through override journals affecting estimates.
Unusual transactions are a classic vehicle for fraudulent reporting, including round-tripping.
Fictitious revenue is often structured as unusual transactions with accommodating counterparties.
Direct verification without warning is the strongest response to suspected diversion of physical assets and cash.
Undisclosed related parties are a common channel for fraudulent reporting structures.
Fictitious revenue frequently involves undisclosed related counterparties.

risks.causes: Management override of controls; ability to post journals outside normal processes; weak independent review of period-end entries.
risks.description: Management or staff use manual journal entries - particularly at period-end, outside hours, or through seldom-used accounts - to misstate reported results, bypassing the controls that govern routine transactions.
risks.inherent_risk_notes: Fraud risk indicators, including those in this library, are red flags that require investigation. They do NOT prove that fraud has occurred, and most indicators have innocent explanations. The auditor's response is extended procedures and scepticism, not accusation.
risks.potential_consequences: Revenue, expenses, assets or liabilities misstated through fictitious or reclassified journals; results shifted between periods; audit trail obscured.
risks.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md
risks.title: Fraudulent financial reporting through manual journal manipulation (management override)

risks.causes: Opportunity created by weak segregation of duties, poor physical controls over assets, and inadequate independent reconciliation.
risks.description: Assets - cash, inventory or other resources - are stolen or diverted for personal use, and the accounting records are falsified to conceal the diversion.
risks.inherent_risk_notes: Fraud risk indicators are red flags that require investigation. They do NOT prove that fraud has occurred, and most indicators have innocent explanations. The auditor's response is extended procedures and scepticism, not accusation.
risks.potential_consequences: Assets overstated (diverted assets still carried, or fictitious assets recorded); losses unrecorded; expenses inflated to absorb the diversion.
risks.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md
risks.title: Misappropriation of assets concealed by falsified records

risks.causes: Intense pressure to meet revenue targets, bonus thresholds, forecasts or covenants; weak cut-off controls; sales team incentives misaligned with proper recognition.
risks.description: Revenue is recorded for transactions that did not occur, or genuine revenue is recognised before the applicable recognition criteria are satisfied, in order to meet targets.
risks.inherent_risk_notes: Fraud risk indicators are red flags that require investigation. They do NOT prove that fraud has occurred, and most indicators have innocent explanations. The auditor's response is extended procedures and scepticism, not accusation.
risks.potential_consequences: Revenue and receivables overstated; profit inflated; subsequent periods correspondingly understated when the premature amounts reverse.
risks.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md
risks.title: Fictitious or premature revenue to meet targets

risks.causes: Pressure to report desired results combined with the subjectivity inherent in estimates; weak independent challenge of assumptions.
risks.description: Management's assumptions in significant accounting estimates are systematically skewed in the direction favourable to reported results - individually within a plausible range, but collectively one-sided.
risks.inherent_risk_notes: Fraud risk indicators are red flags that require investigation. They do NOT prove that fraud has occurred, and most indicators have innocent explanations. An optimistic estimate is not evidence of dishonest intent; only a pattern, combined with other evidence, warrants escalation.
risks.potential_consequences: Carrying amounts misstated (provisions understated, impairments avoided, fair values inflated); profit smoothed or inflated across periods.
risks.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md
risks.title: Systematic management bias in accounting estimates

rules.name: Lack of segregation of duties -> misappropriation fraud risk
rules.rationale: Incompatible functions in one person's hands remove the independent check between a transaction and its concealment - the classic opportunity condition for asset misappropriation. Fraud rules run first (priority 5) so fraud-focused responses are planned before standard procedures.
rules.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

missing_information: Which incompatible functions are combined in which roles.
Whether any compensating controls (e.g. independent review) operate and are evidenced.
Whether the entity's size genuinely prevents segregation.
then.note: Segregation weakness is an opportunity indicator, not evidence of fraud. Respond with extended asset-focused procedures and scepticism, not accusation.

rules.name: Aggressive earnings-linked incentives -> fictitious revenue fraud risk
rules.rationale: Material rewards tied to aggressive targets create the incentive condition for fraudulent revenue reporting. Fraud rules run first (priority 5) so fraud-focused responses are planned before standard procedures.
rules.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

missing_information: How targets are set and whether they are realistically achievable.
The proportion of remuneration tied to the targets.
Whether revenue is the targeted metric or a different measure.
then.note: Target pressure is an incentive indicator, not evidence of fraud. Extend revenue procedures with fraud-focused unpredictability and business-rationale testing.

rules.name: Opaque related-party structures -> journal manipulation fraud risk
rules.rationale: Undocumented related-party structures provide the channels through which manipulated journals and off-book arrangements flow. Fraud rules run first (priority 5).
rules.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

missing_information: The documented business purpose of each structure or vehicle.
The identity of counterparties and whether terms are arm's length.
Which related parties management has disclosed vs omitted.
then.note: Opacity is an opportunity indicator. Respond with journal testing and a related-party completeness search; do not assume the structures are shams.

rules.name: Covenant pressure -> estimate bias fraud risk
rules.rationale: Threatened loss of financing concentrates pressure on period-end balances and the estimates that determine them. Fraud rules run first (priority 5).
rules.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

missing_information: Headroom under each covenant and the consequences of breach.
Timing of covenant tests relative to the reporting date.
Which estimates most affect the covenant ratios.
then.note: Covenant pressure is an incentive indicator. The retrospective estimate review is the key response: look for a pattern of favourable outcomes, not a single optimistic estimate.

rules.name: Finance turnover -> misappropriation fraud risk
rules.rationale: Instability in finance weakens review disciplines and creates gaps in which diversion and concealment go unchallenged. Fraud rules run first (priority 5).
rules.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

missing_information: Reasons for departures and length of vacancies.
Whether handovers were documented and cover is competent.
Which reconciliations and reviews lapsed during gaps.
then.note: Turnover is an opportunity indicator with innocent explanations. Focus extended procedures on periods with weak coverage.

rules.name: Rationalised aggressive accounting -> journal manipulation fraud risk
rules.rationale: A culture that normalises aggressive accounting blurs the boundary between aggressive and improper - the observable form of rationalization. Fraud rules run first (priority 5).
rules.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

missing_information: Specific examples of aggressive positions and their framework basis.
Whether those charged with governance challenged the positions.
Whether policies were changed toward the aggressive end.
then.note: Rationalization is an attitude indicator. Apply heightened scepticism to journals and estimates; an aggressive position is not itself fraud.

rules.name: Weak cash oversight -> misappropriation fraud risk
rules.rationale: Material cash volumes without independent oversight are a direct opportunity for diversion, and cash leaves little trail. Fraud rules run first (priority 5).
rules.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

missing_information: Business reasons for cash intensity and who handles cash.
Whether cash is banked promptly and reconciled independently.
When cash was last independently counted.
then.note: Cash opportunity is a direct misappropriation indicator. Surprise verification is the key response; predictable counts have limited value.

rules.name: No trusted whistleblowing channel -> journal manipulation fraud risk
rules.rationale: Without a safe reporting route, observed wrongdoing - especially involving management - goes unreported, removing a key deterrent and detection channel. Fraud rules run first (priority 5).
rules.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

missing_information: Whether a channel exists on paper and how reports are handled.
Staff perceptions of retaliation risk.
Whether any reports were ever made and investigated.
then.note: Absence of a channel is an opportunity indicator. The auditor compensates with extended procedures and direct enquiry, not with assumptions about management integrity.
